recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core FHIR source follow-up is needed for FHIR-24914 unless a later work-group decision changes the transactional-integrity policy.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive with Modification issue asking the HTTP create/update guidance, or a common location linked by both, to say that servers changing submitted content SHOULD return the stored resource regardless of Prefer or omit the ETag, and that clients receiving a resource in a create/update/patch response SHOULD use returned content as the basis for subsequent update or patch requests; the resolution also noted that out-of-band agreements can make this unnecessary.
initial_application: Git commit 52b757fe6c4dd79e5655b910dd5a43ba0702e980 applied FHIR-24914 by adding the requested notes to source/http.html under Transactional Integrity. The active create and update sections in source/http.html link readers to that Transactional Integrity discussion.
additional_context: The originating Zulip thread records the same rationale: a server may persist changed content, and a client that patches from the originally submitted representation rather than the returned representation can corrupt data. Later HTTP editorial reconciliation for FHIR-39135 corrected a typo in the server bullet without changing the FHIR-24914 rule. Confluence searches found no competing work-group minutes or decision.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The active HTTP page already has the server SHOULD guidance, the client SHOULD guidance, and the out-of-band-agreement caveat in the Transactional Integrity notes.
